markers.reading: The session opens in the afternoon at the Vargold camp, after the earlier ice-worm encounter.

evidence.quote: DM: And now, having traveled some hundreds of miles on your flying castle from the mountains along the Ket River, having fought off a iceworm chasing two isolated lost. [garbled] [garbled] [garbled]? Yeah. [garbled] it's afternoon [garbled].
DM: We're good. Anyway, so now we start in the Vargold camp where you have landed.
Delwath: 1749? Is that right? It's 17 49 by the Drankorian reckoning. Well, presume for Meta.

Delwath: I was gonna say how they track years. I'll, I'll then re-repeat. I never made it up. They probably don't use. Well, Delwath will say 1,749 in the Drankorian reckoning or something, as your people track the years right?

time.basis: Opening narration says afternoon; Delwath later states the current year as 1749. Month and day come only from YAML.

markers.reading: It is about 2:30 p.m. as the party moves into the camp and begins separate conversations.

evidence.quote: Riswynn: What time of day is it at this point, right?
DM: 2 30 in the afternoon.

time.basis: DM answers the question about the current time.

markers.reading: The party completes a short rest in the course of the camp conversations; Riswynn explicitly rests while the others act as ambassadors.

evidence.quote: Riswynn: Riswynn's gonna [garbled] on a stone and pray, and cast spells to heal herself and restore magic slots and things, so that if something bad comes swooping in the sky she's not limping around all soggy in it.
DM: I mean, you can take a short rest during your sort of conversation, so you can roll hit dice, and do any.
Riswynn: She, she trusts that Delwath, Wellby, and Kenzo are being good ambassadors, and she'll hear about it later. So she's gonna deal with the creaks.

DM: The North. Strange North. So at this point you all reconvene at like 4 in the afternoon. Something like that, to plan and discuss. Having taken a short rest, I would say, in the course of these conversations, and catching up, the sun beginning to sink low in the sky. Torsten and Yota, increasingly nervous and basically asking, like, "We can pack up in 30 min. Like, what do you think? Should we stay, or should we run?"
Delwath: I mean did, but if it comes, it comes. But we could run. I mean, I'm not in my best shape, but I can handle it. I did a short rest, and I'm back to— Do you still have high level spell slots?
DM: Yeah, you got a short rest.

duration.basis: short-rest convention; later DM narration explicitly awards the completed rest during the conversations

markers.note: This rest is contained in the conversation period before the 4 p.m. reunion, not an extra hour after it.

markers.reading: Wellby enters ancestral memories: ancient coastal landings, animal-speaking halflings, and later human settlement, before Drankor.

evidence.quote: DM: So Wellby now is trying to reach back into the past of the halflings and kind of get a feel for the land and a vision of who these halflings are, and how they ended up here. And, and what you see is, you kind of reach back into the past. Just expending your [garbled]— Expending your, expending your use, your ability to sort of perceive the history of your ancestors. Do you see? You see 3 sort of flashes of of images of of lore. And the first you can tell is very long ago, because the image is almost— It's almost like the memory itself is frayed and faded. And it's— And you, you've experienced this when you were younger, sailing on the Green Sea. Like, halflings have been sailing on the Green Sea for forever, basically. Like, this was a, you know, this was kind of one of the things halflings did as soon as they were created by the First Ones is travel the Green Sea.

DM: And then just time passing. And again you get the sense that this was all like long ago, like even before humans came, like before, certainly before Drankor, before, you know, the Empire started spreading, anything like that. But humans did come. Humans much like the people that you are talking to now, the the Vargold. And they also somehow learned to speak with the animals, and brought with them some divinity of some kind. They brought with them animals within them, animal spirits, animal gods, and they learned how to kind of ask those animal spirits for protection, and the humans made the animals stronger and the animals made the humans stronger.

DM: And as they settled and traveled in the land, the halflings were curious. And so they learned the magic of shapeshifting that seem to lie heavy on this land, some unusual power, some unusual strength of that particular magic from growing from the humans and the spirits that they brought with them. And sometimes some leave and sometimes new halflings come. Not everybody stays forever in this land, and over the generations the newcomers become assimilated and learn. And over time those who leave lose the spirit. That's their story.

relative.anchor: Drankor and the spread of its empire

time.basis: The ancestral-memory narration explicitly places these images before Drankor; no numerical date or elapsed adventure duration is supplied.

markers.reading: The party returns from separate investigations and the ancestral-memory narration to a reunion at about 4 p.m., with the short rest already completed.

evidence.quote: DM: The North. Strange North. So at this point you all reconvene at like 4 in the afternoon. Something like that, to plan and discuss. Having taken a short rest, I would say, in the course of these conversations, and catching up, the sun beginning to sink low in the sky. Torsten and Yota, increasingly nervous and basically asking, like, "We can pack up in 30 min. Like, what do you think? Should we stay, or should we run?"

time.basis: DM says reconvening at like 4 in the afternoon, something like that.

markers.reading: Wellby flies toward the distant dragon for fifteen minutes, confirms the sighting through his spyglass, and returns; only the outward leg has a stated duration.

evidence.quote: DM: You can fly closer. You can fly an hour a day.
Wellby: Sure. I'll fly that direction for 15 min. I'll whip out that spyglass that I keep around. Oh, yeah, it's definitely a dragon. Yeah, I'll fly back right quick.
DM: It's, so, It hasn't turned south yet. It's clearly, like, it looks like it's, it kind of looks like a, like a vulture soaring at the moment.

duration.basis: Accepted scouting action states fifteen minutes outward; return is confirmed but not timed.

markers.note: Do not double the outward duration into an asserted thirty-minute round trip.

markers.reading: Loading the Vargold camp onto the hidden ship takes about half an hour, while the dragon draws closer.

evidence.quote: DM: So everybody's piling onto the ship. The camp is rapidly disappearing. You know, everybody is grateful, a little bit, like, disturbed by the Orcs, almost looking at Kenzo, like, "Am I actually gonna see a dragon?"

DM: The camp is now almost gone. Faldrak's like, you know, fluttering around as everybody is like this huge crowd of people descending on the ship, like, "Is there space for everybody? Like, let's get them stowed. You might have to fly. Nobody hanging off the edge."

DM: And this is taking about half an hour, and at this point all of you can clearly see the dragon growing bigger. Not particularly fast. Like, it seems like it's just sort of curious, like, "What was that thing that I saw?"

duration.basis: DM explicitly says this is taking about half an hour.

markers.reading: At the makeshift ambush camp, the sun is setting and twilight provides dim light.

evidence.quote: DM: So you've got a campfire and you've got a tent quickly set up.

DM: And now it's, the sun is setting. It's twilight, so everything's dim light but still visible. Right, so not impossible to see, but it will help you hide, for those of you are hiding. So where is where is everybody?

time.basis: DM narration; calendar month/day are not independently spoken.

markers.reading: After harvesting the dragon, the sun has fully set and the party returns to the ship.

evidence.quote: DM: After, as the sun is now fully set, and the dragon's carcass is beginning to melt and steam. Anyway, the Wall of Fire is gone. You return to camp, I guess, or return to the ship, I guess.

DM: And as you return, you, I mean, you don't [garbled]. I guess the, the giant is now visible, because— But otherwise, like everything is still— The ship is still hidden. Still this, like, hill and trees around it. And as you, as you approach, you see, like, faces start to poke out of the, out of the hill. One, and then 2 more. And then 5 more. And then there's just like cheering. Like 20 faces sticking out over the hill, looking at you as you return, board your ship again, like, everybody is just super grateful, happy. Torsten comes up and says, "Did not think it could be done. There is anything we can do for you, anything, just ask it, and it will be so."

time.basis: DM narration; calendar month/day are not independently spoken.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: 1749 is independently spoken at u0460-u0469. March 21 is inherited from YAML; no month or day is independently spoken.
yamlCheck.explanation: Played events run from the afternoon arrival to the return after sunset on one day. The earlier journey and ice-worm fight are recalled, the ancestral memories are a separate historical frame, and the two-week stay and onward journey are future plans at u2463-u2484. The midnight comment at u2481-u2484 is table wrap-up, not an adventure date advance. No overnight rest is narrated.
